title: Onlay- vs. Inlay-Type Patellofemoral Arthroplasty: a multi-centric, retrospective, comparative study
summary:
If patients suffer from joint wear exclusively between the patella and the femur (the patellofemoral joint), it is possible to replace only this part of the knee joint with a surface replacement (a prosthesis).
There are two groups of different designs of patellofemoral prostheses: onlay patellofemoral prostheses and inlay patellofemoral prostheses.
In this study, we retrospectively investigate whether there is a significant difference in treatment outcome between these two designs.
conditions: Outcome of patellofemoral prostheses in patients with isolated patellofemoral osteoarthritis

interventions.name: Patients, who received an Onlay-PFA between 2010 and 2022
Patients, who received an Inlay-PFA between 2010 and 2022

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients who received an isolated patellofemoral arthroplasty between 2010 and 2023
- Follow-up-period of at least 2 years
Exclusion criteria:
-	Additional surgery on the ipsilateral knee unrelated to the patellofemoral joint
Patients with concomitant patellofemoral alignment procedures (during the same anaesthesia) will not be excluded (lateral retinacular lengthening or release,
rotational osteotomy around the knee, tuberosity transfer, medial patellofemoral ligament plasty).
